title: Multi-Domain Deception Detection Empirical Benchmark
description: Comprehensive comparative evaluation across Hotel Reviews (Ott et al.) and Personal Statements (Pérez-Rosas & Mihalcea 2015)

personal_statements.splitting_strategy: Contributor-grouped (103 held-out test authors, zero contributor overlap)

exp1_in_domain_personal_statements.experiment_name: Exp 1: Personal Statements In-Domain (Pérez-Rosas & Mihalcea 2015 Held-out Test)

exp2_cross_domain_hotel_to_ps.experiment_name: Exp 2: Zero-Shot Cross-Domain (Hotel Model evaluated on Personal Statements Test)
exp2_cross_domain_hotel_to_ps.finding: Demonstrates near-chance transfer (48.3% accuracy, 0.4957 AUC), proving that hotel-review deception markers do not generalize zero-shot to first-person personal statements.

exp3_cross_domain_ps_to_hotel.experiment_name: Exp 3: Zero-Shot Cross-Domain (Personal Statement Model evaluated on Hotel Reviews Test)
exp3_cross_domain_ps_to_hotel.finding: Demonstrates chance transfer (49.7% accuracy, 0.5213 AUC), confirming that personal narrative markers do not directly translate to commercial hospitality opinion spam.

hotel_evaluation.experiment_name: Exp 4A: Joint Multi-Domain Model -> Evaluated on Hotel Reviews Test Set

personal_statement_evaluation.experiment_name: Exp 4B: Joint Multi-Domain Model -> Evaluated on Personal Statements Test Set

exp4_joint_multi_domain.finding: The joint model preserves strong in-domain hotel performance (85.0% accuracy, 0.9307 AUC) while concurrently attaining in-domain personal statement accuracy (62.8% accuracy, 0.6562 AUC).

scientific_limitations_and_disclaimer: Notice: Personal statement deception exhibits modest separability (62.55% accuracy) using lexical n-grams, consistent with published academic findings in Pérez-Rosas & Mihalcea (2015). Cross-domain zero-shot experiments (~48-50%) show that text deception is heavily domain-dependent and context-specific. Models evaluate statistical resemblance to training data and do not constitute universal lie detection.
